credit: Written for the app from the Emerald City data, drawn only from L. Frank Baum's Oz books, which are public domain in the US.

entries.title: Soft rain
entries.text: Rain in the Emerald City is soft and warm and never lasts long; the green marble streets shine, the emeralds set in them glitter, and children splash in the gutters until the sun comes out.

entries.title: A dusting of snow
entries.text: A rare light snow on a winter morning makes the green city white for an hour, and people come out just to look before it melts.

entries.title: A warm day
entries.text: On a warm day people take their afternoon tea in the gardens, the fountains in the palace grounds are crowded, and the green lemonade carts have queues.

entries.title: Spring in Oz
entries.text: In spring the orchards along the yellow brick road blossom, the gardens of the city come into flower, and the Gillikin families plant their purple-trimmed allotments.

entries.title: Summer in Oz
entries.text: In summer the long warm evenings are spent outdoors, puppet shows play Dorothy's adventures on Market Square, and the first fruit comes in from the farms.

entries.title: Autumn in Oz
entries.text: In autumn the cider barns press apples for sweet new cider, sold by the jug from the taverns, and fires are lit in the tavern hearths on the cool evenings.

entries.title: Winter in Oz
entries.text: Winter in the city is short cool days and cosy evenings, and since nobody in Oz grows old or falls ill, nobody minds the cold much.

entries.title: Early morning
entries.text: Before sunrise Oven Street smells of bread from the bakehouses and dairies, and the wagons from all four countries roll in to Market Square.

entries.title: Afternoon tea
entries.text: In the afternoon many people stop work for tea, cakes and bread and butter, often in a garden or by the window. In Oz people work half the time and play half the time.

entries.title: Evening in the city
entries.text: In the evening the city glows green under its lamps, families stroll around Pump Square's bandstand, and homesick travellers are told "there is no place like home".

entries.title: The Gate Quarter
entries.text: At the great gate the Guardian of the Gates still keeps a box of green spectacles from the Wizard's day, though under Ozma nobody has to wear them.

entries.title: The palace
entries.text: At the Royal Palace the soldier with the long green whiskers keeps the door, and he is the one to ask for anything.

entries.title: Market Square
entries.text: On Market Square wagons from all four countries unload fruit, grain and cloth, everyone takes what they need without money, and children buy green popcorn from the carts.

entries.title: Winkie Street
entries.text: On Winkie Street the yellow Winkie tinsmiths who once mended the Tin Woodman still make and mend kettles, lanterns and oil-cans.

entries.title: No money in Oz
entries.text: There is no money in Oz: people work for the good of all and take what they need from the shops and storehouses without paying.

entries.title: Work in the Emerald City
entries.text: Work in the Emerald City is done for the good of all and never all day: half the time is for play, and nobody is scolded for stopping to watch a puppet show.
